sources.title: The Age of Spiritual Machines — Ray Kurzweil (1999)
sources.locator: P02 Health care in 2009, telemedicine bullet

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source on Sources for attribution limits.

strict.criterion: Ordinary telemedicine routinely incorporates remote tactile/haptic physical examination alongside audio and video.
strict.rationale: Phone and video telemedicine became widespread by 2021 (37% of US adults), but remotely conveyed tactile examination was neither common in 2009 nor part of standard telemedicine practice in 2026.
changedConditions: Enforces the explicit remote-tactile examination requirement

evidence.title: CDC: Telemedicine use among adults, United States, 2021
evidence.note: 37% of US adults used phone or video telemedicine in 2021. Does not establish widespread tactile remote examination.

evidence.title: Paterson: Feel the Presence—Technologies of Touch and Distance
evidence.note: Describes 2002 Boston–London virtual handshake and networked force feedback; supports emerging remote touch, not full-body realism.

reference.criterion: Remote examinations using sight, sound and tactile sensing are widely used.
reference.rationale: Audio/video telemedicine and remote-device demonstrations did not make the full visual-auditory-haptic package widespread in 2009. The 37% US adult telemedicine-use figure for 2021 establishes ordinary audio/video care, but not widespread remotely conveyed tactile examination.

broader.rationale: Audio/video use reached an unmistakably common level by 2021.
